title: Lean SDP-uniqueness wiring for the atlas entries
html:
Remark. Lean SDP-uniqueness wiring for the atlas entries

SDP uniqueness, Lean side

What is certified: the abstract framework demonstration of T_w uniqueness at the empty-constraint SDP for a nucleus's strand count. The real per-nucleus SDP (with non-empty constraints from the mass formula and multi-term cost) is per-nucleus substantive open work.

Within that scope, each atlas entry has a corresponding sorry-free SDP-uniqueness theorem on the Lean side. Take ^4He: with mass number A = 4 the strand count is n = 3A = 12, and the canonical T_w knot operator's uniqueness at the empty-constraint SDP demonstration level is certified by the single parameterised statement

\texttt{nucleus\_uniqueness\_closed}\ (3A)\ : \ \text{(sorry-free, axiom-free)}

instantiated at 3A = 12. The same statement, supplied by the parameterised NucleusEmptySDPUniqueness module, covers any nucleus once A (equivalently n = 3A) is fixed.

Named wrappers expose this at four granularity layers — from the ten the tracked nuclei, through per-element and per-stable-isotope coverage, down to the generic module valid for any n : \mathbb{N}:

Granularity Lean file Coverage
tracked nuclei Applied<Nucleus>Uniqueness.lean (10 files) ^2H, ^3H, ^3He, ^4He, ^6Li, ^9Be, ^{11}B, ^{12}C, ^{14}N, ^{16}O
Per-element (AME2020 ref) PeriodicTableUniqueness.lean 118 elements H..Og
Per-stable-isotope StableIsotopeUniqueness.lean 252 stable nuclides H..Bi
Generic NucleusEmptySDPUniqueness.lean Any n : \mathbb{N}

To cite a specific entry, use qou:QOU.BraidKnot.<isotope>_uniqueness_closed; for atoms outside the named-isotope set, apply @nucleus_uniqueness_closed (3*A) directly with the atlas A. Element symbols follow AtomicMass.lean, with an _el suffix where the short symbol collides with a reserved Lean identifier (e.g. n_el_uniqueness_closed for nitrogen).
